deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Move from unprompted appreciation to the occasion rule, the evidence gap, the need-state audience, one explicit design brief, one solution sentence, one live demo and one team-authored handoff.
deck.evidence_rule: The displayed participant ratings and percentages are disclosed in the slide footers as temporary rehearsal data because Ethan explicitly requested presentable test values; they must be replaced before the judged pitch. Published studies support only the adjacent channel mechanisms, not the practice values, plotted positions, Goldilocks gap or product superiority.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: An unprompted-appreciation question becomes an occasion rule, a visibly unproven format gap, an evidence-to-solution deduction, one live giving ritual and a real thank-you object for the room.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity and team, then move immediately.

visual.composition: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark on white, with the approved team name, team number and confirmed member names. Do not add narrative copy.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Name the team and move.
Blocked until team number and member-name spelling are confirmed.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time you showed someone appreciation or gratitude?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recall the last time they initiated an unprompted act of appreciation before the team names the problem.

visual.composition: One full-frame question ending with `appreciation or gratitude?` Do not put the birthday or event clarification on the slide. Do not mention letters, because that reveals a solution format before the problem is established. No counterpoint, supporting sentence or raise-hands prompt.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Ask the visible sender-framed appreciation-or-gratitude question and pause briefly. Then say aloud that birthdays, celebrations and major events do not count.
Do not mention letters, ask for raised hands or add the removed `we have never had more ways to talk` counterpoint.
A pause or difficulty remembering opens the story; it is not evidence.
Cultural transmission and fear of social judgment remain mechanisms to research, not facts to state.

motion.description: One question appears once; no staged subtext.

slides.claim: We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the problem as an expression barrier, not missing care.

visual.composition: One plain problem statement in the established navy-and-white colour system. No Chloe attribution, mentor quote, persona, explanatory paragraph or orange detour.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
Say that appreciation can already exist while expressing it on an ordinary day still feels out of the ordinary.
Treat this as the team's current problem framing, not a prevalence finding.

motion.description: Emphasise `show it` only after the full statement lands.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the working unwritten rule and the design question it creates.

visual.composition: Birthdays, farewells and milestones each visibly supply permission; an ordinary Tuesday supplies no prompt and an unexpected appreciation text can trigger `Is everything okay?`. Close with one line: `How might we create that permission on an ordinary day?`

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.

Ask why showing appreciation appears to require a socially recognised time. Use the ordinary-Tuesday example: through conventional messaging, an unexpected appreciation message can feel worrying because it sits outside the norm.
The rule and reaction are working hypotheses; their prevalence, boundaries and exceptions still require primary research.

motion.description: Show occasion prompts, then the unprompted ordinary day, then the How Might We.

slides.claim: The possible Goldilocks gap combines high recipient impact, low mental and physical friction, and enough frequency for an ordinary day.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the three rating dimensions across three broad form families, the published mechanisms beside them, and the combination the team is trying to reach.

visual.composition: An impact-versus-friction map where each dot's size encodes how frequently that form family is received. Reveal quick text; voice note / video call; and handwritten letter / physical gift. Beside each active point show the bounded conclusions for both members of a grouped family; the grouping simplifies the pitch and does not claim equivalence. Keep numeric ratings for page 6. Finish on an unboxed `goldilocks zone` for high impact, low friction and repeatability. Use #94A550 for the accent and a darker paired green for small accent text. The footer identifies the grouped positions as temporary.

speaker_notes: Timing: 60 seconds; this remains the longest evidence slide.
Walk through quick text, voice/video and letter/gift as presentation families; name the bounded findings shown beside each point without claiming the paired forms are equivalent.
Do not read numeric ratings; page 6 owns the comparison table.
Replace every grouped position, point size and all temporary figures on slides 6 and 8 with documented results before the judged pitch.
The matched-format test must still compare the individual forms and the prototype before the Goldilocks gap can become a result.

motion.description: Reveal the three channel families with their unboxed paper conclusions, then reveal the Goldilocks combination on the fourth click.

slides.audience_takeaway: Read the actual What, Why and How findings at presentation distance without relying on explanatory subtext.

visual.composition: Preserve the original three-column What / Why / How format. What shows 82%; Why shows 71%; How contains a three-row table that fills the remaining height of the right column for quick text, voice note / video call and handwritten letter / physical gift across impact, friction and frequency out of five. On a fourth click, circle letter/gift impact, quick-text friction and voice/video frequency to show the three qualities the team wants to combine. A footer discloses that all grouped figures are temporary and do not establish equivalence.

speaker_notes: Timing: 40 seconds.
Move through What and Why, reveal the three grouped form families, then explain that each has strengths but no family captures all three.
Click once more to circle the three source qualities: letter/gift impact, text friction and voice/video frequency.
Every value is temporary rehearsal data. Replace it after recruitment, method, sample, wording, analysis, exact results, exceptions and limitations are recorded.
Psychology on text meaningfulness, synchronous voice/video and perceived effort supports only the channel mechanisms; it cannot validate these grouped figures or equivalence.

motion.description: Reveal What, Why and the compact How table, then circle the three qualities the solution will combine.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the first target as people whose desired gesture falls between an ordinary text and a physical letter or gift.

visual.composition: Replace the invented grandmother-granddaughter persona with overlapping Goldilocks rings. One ring says a text can feel too casual; the other says a letter or gift can carry too much friction. Put university students, long-distance connections, close friends and close family inside the green double-ring overlap as included examples, not exclusive demographics or validated segments.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Define the target by the situation: they already care, an ordinary text feels too casual, and a letter or gift feels disproportionate or impractical.
Use university students, long-distance connections, close friends and close family as included examples only.
This remains a working need-state, not validated demand, market size or a research-derived persona.

motion.description: Reveal the two overlapping need rings, reveal the green Goldilocks overlap, then name the included relationship contexts.

slides.claim: If the expression gap exists and ordinary-day appreciation feels awkward, then normalise the act by aiming for gift-level impact with digital-level friction and repeatability.
slides.audience_takeaway: Follow the evidence deduction into one explicit product requirement before the solution reveal.

visual.composition: Preserve the high-contrast If / And / Then chain. Add a fourth unboxed `Therefore` line at the bottom: create the impact of gift-giving with the low friction and repeatability of everyday digital contact. Use the same temporary 82% and 71% rehearsal figures as slide 6, disclosed in the footer, until real results replace them.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
For rehearsal, connect the temporary What and Why figures, name normalising ordinary-day appreciation as the outcome, then state the product requirement in the Therefore line.
Replace the two temporary percentages before the judged pitch. The desired outcome and Goldilocks combination remain a design deduction, not a validated result.

motion.description: Reveal If, And, Then and the added Therefore requirement in order.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies is a private digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the proposed solution and intended comparative advantage in one sentence before the live demonstration.

visual.composition: One large centred sentence only: `Warm & Fuzzies is a private digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.` Emphasise the two borrowed qualities in the green accent. Remove the phone screenshot, product-name lockup, mechanism subtext and prototype footer.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Read or closely paraphrase the single solution sentence, then switch immediately to the running prototype.
Treat thoughtfulness plus ease as the product proposition that the demo makes legible, not as a validated superiority claim or measured outcome.

motion.description: Show the complete solution sentence at once, then stop deck motion for the live demo.

slides.audience_takeaway: Watch one complete working sender-to-receiver journey rather than a narrated feature tour.

visual.composition: A dark holding slide containing only `Let us show you.` Then leave the deck and begin the live prototype. No process verbs, instruction line, screenshot sequence or video.

speaker_notes: Timing: 100 seconds.
Switch to the live prototype. Show only the critical path: compose one object, seal it, choose its travel, create the link, open as receiver, then keep, close or remove without replying.

Explain the relevant process decision while it appears: why the object shows effort, why sealing creates closure, why the link reduces receiving friction and why the receiver controls the ending. Keep the emphasis on the research logic, not a separate process diary.
Demonstrate only working states. Do not claim delivery infrastructure, verified identity, encrypted privacy, ownership, permanent storage or lower awkwardness.
Use a preloaded static or local fallback only if the live path fails; never spend pitch time showing both a video and the live demo.

motion.description: Deck motion stops while the presenter demonstrates the working prototype; return only after the receiver outcome is visible.

slides.claim: We made something for you, too.
slides.audience_takeaway: Receive a real team-authored thank-you through the same flow, voluntarily and without reply pressure.

visual.composition: The final handoff uses a real approved photo or selfie of the team making the object, a real thank-you object with contributions from the team, and the verified live QR and URL. Include an equally clear no-device fallback. Do not ship a generic placeholder card as the final state.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Thank the hosts and room, say the team made this object for them, and invite them to open it privately and optionally. No reply is expected.
Blocked until the real team photo has consent, the team-authored object is complete, the deployed receiver URL is tested on a second device, and the QR is verified at presentation distance.
A scan, smile, applause or emotional reaction demonstrates the handoff only; it is not impact evidence.

motion.description: Reveal the real team photo, then the verified handoff card. No separate conclusion slide follows.
